Valley of Decision
VAL-ee of dih-SIZH-un
proper noun
From the Hebrew 'emeq he-charuts, “the valley of decision,” the noun charuts springing from charats, to cut, sharpen, and so to determine; the margin reads “concision” or “threshing.” It is Joel’s name for the valley of Jehoshaphat, “the LORD judgeth.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Joel lifts the eye of the church to a valley that no map can fix, the valley of decision, which is the valley of Jehoshaphat, where the LORD declares, “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down…and will plead with them there” (Joe 3:2). It is the floor of the last assize. The prophet cries, “Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision” (Joe 3:14). The word rendered decision carries the sense of threshing, the sharp stroke that parts the wheat from the chaff, and so the valley is no place of man’s deliberation but of God’s determination. Here the Judge of all the earth does right. Before Him shall be gathered all nations, and He shall separate them one from another, “as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats” (Mat 25:32); the books are opened, and the dead are judged every man according to his works (Rev 20:12). This is a sober word, not a rumor to be softened. The valley of decision teaches that history bends toward a reckoning, that God’s long patience is not slumber, and that the day is near. Yet the elect need not fear the threshingfloor, for their names are written in the Lamb’s book of life, and the Shepherd who divides has already numbered His own. Flee, then, to Christ before the sickle falls.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Joel’s name for the valley of Jehoshaphat, where the LORD gathers all nations to judgment (Joe 3:14); the floor of the last assize, where the wheat is threshed from the chaff.

expand to see more

VALLEY OF DECISION, the valley of Jehoshaphat where the LORD judgeth the nations (Joe 3:2, 14).

The Hebrew carries the sense of threshing, the stroke that parts wheat from chaff.

Here all nations are gathered, and the day of the LORD is near.

The Judge separates the sheep from the goats, and the books are opened.

A sober figure of the final judgment, from which the elect flee to Christ.

📖 Key Scripture

Joe 3:14 — "Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision."

Joe 3:2 — "I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land."

Mat 25:32 — "And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:"

Rev 20:12 — "And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The age dismisses a coming day of judgment as myth or metaphor; the valley of decision recalls the church to the certainty of the great assize.

expand to see more

The great corruption of the present hour is the quiet deletion of the last judgment. Men will speak of a God of love while striking from their creed the day when He shall judge the world in righteousness, and the valley of decision is folded into figure, as though Joel spoke only of inward choices and not of the LORD gathering all nations to be judged. But the prophet is plain: the day of the LORD is near, and the threshing is real.

The recovery is a sober and unflinching eschatology. Scripture sets a day, and appoints a Judge, and opens the books; the dead, small and great, shall stand before God, and be judged according to their works (Rev 20:12), the sheep parted from the goats (Mat 25:32). This is no manufactured terror but the settled testimony of the word. Let the church preach it whole—wrath to come and refuge in Christ—that sinners may flee to the Shepherd before the sickle falls, and that the saints may lift up their heads, knowing their names are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From charats, to cut, sharpen, and so to decide or determine; the noun names a strict, sharp-edged verdict.

expand to see more

'emeq he-charuts — the valley of decision (Joe 3:14).

charats — to cut, sharpen, determine, decide.

The margin renders it “concision” or “threshing.”

So the valley is a threshingfloor of nations.

Jehoshaphat, its other name, means “the LORD judgeth.”

Usage

"Multitudes gather in the valley of decision, for the day of the LORD is near."

"The valley of decision is the floor of the last judgment."

"There the LORD threshes the nations, parting the wheat from the chaff."
